Course Description
This course, "Principles of Programming Languages," provides a foundational understanding of the core
concepts and paradigms of programming languages. Students will explore the historical development, syntax,
semantics, and pragmatics of various languages. Key topics include formal language theory, syntax analysis,
data types, type systems, and control structures. The course also covers different programming paradigms—
imperative, declarative, functional, logic, and object-oriented—along with advanced topics like concurrency
and domain-specific languages. By the end, students will be able to evaluate and apply these concepts
effectively.
Course Outcomes
CO No. Statement
1 Understand the historical context and evolution of programming languages and categorize
languages based on different paradigms.
2 Analyze and apply formal syntax and semantics to programming language constructs.
3 Understand different data types, type systems, and abstraction mechanisms in programming
languages.
4 Apply various control structures and subprogram mechanisms in programming language design.
5 Compare and contrast different programming paradigms and apply paradigm-specific features to
solve programming problems.

Course Content
Unit No 1 Title of Unit: Introduction to Programming Hours 6 CO BTL
Languages
 History and Evolution: Early languages, development of modern languages. 1 1, 2
 Language Paradigms: Imperative, functional, logic, and object-oriented programming
languages.
 Language Design and Implementation: Syntax, semantics, and pragmatics.
 Translators: Compilers, interpreters, and hybrid systems.
Unit No 2 Title of Unit: Syntax and Semantics Hours 6
 Syntax: Lexical analysis, parsing, and syntax trees. 2 1, 2
 Formal Language Theory: Grammars, regular expressions, and context-free grammars.
 Semantics: Operational, denotational, and axiomatic semantics.
 Language Constructs: Expressions, statements, and control structures.
Unit No 3 Title of Unit: Data Types and Abstraction Hours 6
 Primitive Data Types: Integer, float, boolean, character. 3 1, 2
 Composite Data Types: Arrays, records, unions.
 Abstract Data Types: Encapsulation and modularity.
 Type Systems: Static vs. dynamic typing, strong vs. weak typing.
Unit No 4 Title of Unit: Control Structures and Subprograms Hours 6
 Control Structures: Conditional statements, loops, and control flow mechanisms. 4 1, 2
 Subprograms: Functions, procedures, and coroutines.
 Parameter Passing: By value, by reference, and by name.
 Recursion: Concepts and implementation.
Unit No 5 Title of Unit: Programming Paradigms Hours 6
 Imperative Programming: Variable assignment, loops, and procedure calls. 5 1, 2
 Functional Programming: First-class functions, higher-order functions, and recursion.
 Logic Programming: Facts, rules, and queries.
 Object-Oriented Programming: Classes, objects, inheritance, and polymorphism.

Course Description
The Python programming course is essential for the degree program as it provides fundamental to advanced skills
vital for contemporary software development. Python's flexibility and rich library ecosystem prepare students for
diverse tech careers in areas like data science, web development, and automation. Practical projects and
assessments ensure students can apply their knowledge effectively, bridging theory with real-world applications.
Course Outcomes
CO No. Statement
1 Gain proficiency in Python syntax, basic data structures, control structures (loops, conditionals),
and functions/modules to write efficient scripts and programs.
2 Learn to design and implement classes, utilize inheritance and polymorphism, and apply object-
oriented concepts to solve complex programming problems.
3 Master functional programming techniques (lambda functions, map, filter, reduce), exception
handling, decorators, and generators for efficient and robust coding practices.
4 Familiarize with popular libraries like NumPy and Pandas for data manipulation, Matplotlib for
visualization, and Flask/Django for web development to create robust applications.
5 Acquire skills in multithreading, multiprocessing, socket programming, and basics of data science
and machine learning using Python libraries like scikit-learn and TensorFlow.

Course Description
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to web technologies, covering the fundamental principles of
HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for creating and styling web pages. Students will learn to develop interactive web
applications using ReactJS, and server-side programming with Node.js and MySQL. The course also explores
the MEAN stack (MongoDB, Express.js, Angular, Node.js) for full-stack development. Emphasis is placed on
both front-end and back-end development, including web design, form validation, and database connectivity.
By the end of the course, students will be equipped with the skills to build dynamic and responsive web
applications.
Course Outcomes
CO No. Statement
1 Understand and apply the fundamentals of web technology and HTML, including structuring
HTML documents and styling them with CSS.
2 Develop interactive web applications using JavaScript, focusing on DOM manipulation, event
handling, and form validation.
3 Build dynamic and responsive front-end applications using ReactJS, managing state and props, and
integrating with backend services.
4 Create and manage server-side applications using Node.js, and perform database operations with
MySQL to develop full-stack web applications.
5 Develop full-stack web applications using the MEAN stack, integrating MongoDB, Express.js,
Angular, and Node.js to manage the entire application lifecycle.

Course Description
To learn critical and creative thinking of models and the components of research with the necessary skills and
knowledge to conduct high-quality research in the fields, fostering their ability to contribute significantly to
academic and professional communities.
Course Outcomes
CO No. Statement
1 Gain a solid understanding of research methodology, including objectives, types, and scientific research
processes.
2 Learn effective data collection methods such as observation, interviews, surveys, and questionnaire design.
3 Understand criteria and types of sampling designs, including probability and non-probability
methods.
4 Apply large and small sample tests, including t-tests, F-tests, and Chi-Square tests for statistical analysis.
5 Improve skills in writing and interpreting research reports, theses, and journal publications.

Unit No I Introduction to Research Methodology 12 Hours CO BTL
Introduction to Research Methodology: Meaning, Objectives, Motivation in Research, 1 1,3
Types, Approaches, Importance, Research Methodology, Scientific Research, Process, Criteria
for Good Research, Problems Encountered, Defining Research Problem, Developing Research
Proposal,
Research Design: Meaning, Need, Features, Important, Six P of Research
Data Collection Method- Primary Data- Observation Method, Personal Interview, Telephonic
Interview, Mail Survey, Questionnaire Design.
Unit No II Sampling Design 12 Hours 2 1,2,4
Implications, Steps Criteria for Sampling Procedure, Characteristics of Good Sample Design,
Different Types of Sample Design, Different Types of Sample Design- (a) Probability Sampling
Like Simple Random, System Random, Systematic Random, Stratified, Cluster.(B) Non
Probability Sampling Like Quota, Judgmental, Convenience
Unit No III Large and small Sample Test 12 Hours 3 3,4,5
Large Sample Test: Definition of Hypothesis, Basic Concepts- Null Hypothesis and
Alternative, The Level of Significance, Type I and Type II Errors, Two Tailed and One Tailed,
Power of Test, Testing of Mean, Testing of Differences Between Two Means, Testing of
Proportion of Difference Between Two Proportion Limitations of Hypothesis Testing.
Small Sample Test: Idea of Degree of Freedom, Test Significance Based Upon T and F
Statistic-Testing of Mean, Testing of Difference Between Two Means, Testing of Equality of
Variances, Chi-Square Test.
Unit No IV CHI-Square Test for Large Samples 12 Hours 4 3,4,5
CHI-Square Test for Large Samples: Definition of Chi-Square, Limitations of Chi-Square
Test, and Chi-Square Test As a Test of Goodness of Fit and As a Test of Independence,
Yates’s Correction and Its Application,
Analysis of Variance (ANOVA): Concept, One Way ANOVA, and ANOVA in Test in Latin
Square Design.

Pre-Writing Considerations. Meaning and Technique of Interpretation,
Different Types of Report Writing, formats of Report Writing, Thesis
Writing, formats of Publication in Research Journals.
